Argument for “Beggar Role as Advantageous and Sustainable”

1. Direct, Recurring Material Benefits  
  a. Valuable Gifts Only Available to Beggars  
    – “Oh, splendid idea … a bar of chocolate … universal language” (<invalid_quote>‘Why not give him a bar of chocolate, then?’ … Skkiru ate the candy then and there. Chocolate increased the body’s resistance to weather.</invalid_quote>) (ch. 11)  
       * Chocolate is rare, expensive, and now unavailable on Snaddra except via visitors. His repeated use of the term “increased resistance” implies he plans to beg more, knowing its life‐sustaining effects.  
    – Beggar status grants him “first crack” at Terran gifts and the best hut: <quote>"We have prepared our best hut for you, noble sirs,</quote> (ch. 12)  
       * This “best hut” would be denied to metal‐workers or any citizen living “aboveground” on primitive terms.  
  b. Superior Mobility to Gain Prestige and Supplies  
    – Skkiru’s “wrecked air‐car” pontoons: he exploits technology under the guise of “primitive land transport,” arriving “long before” official greeters (<quote>because what could be more primitive</quote>) (ch. 10)  
       * Demonstrates that, as a beggar, he has freedom to deploy hidden assets—to both impress the Terrans and secure early alms.  
    – If his plan were hopeless, he would not waste time retrieving pontoons or enduring weather, yet he “stifled the quiver in his toe” and persisted.  

2. Institutional Support and Long‐Term Security  
  a. Government Pension and Structured Role  
    – “Bbulas would probably have to arrange some sort of pension for him” (<invalid_quote> he could not expect Skkiru's  patriotism to extend to abnormal limits.</invalid_quote>) (ch. 11)  
    – Annual “rain dance” and feast days ensure regular Terran visits to maintain the ruse (<invalid_quote>“this ceremony… is to stop rain”</invalid_quote>) (ch. 13)  
       * Continual need for “primitive” culture guarantees earnings. Without beggars to enhance the primitive façade, Terrans will leave, cutting off imports.  
  b. Option to Emigrate Exists but Is Rejected  
    – Skkiru refuses to “emigrate” or “play metals‐worker” despite starvation risk because “that would not be playing the game … Besides, … he wouldn’t be able to see Larhgan.” (ch. 11)  
       * His voluntary choice to remain in beggar caste underpins his acceptance and belief in its viability.  

3. Strategic Hope for Upward Mobility via Terran “Primitive” Romance  
  a. Leveraging Beggar “Romance” Tradition  
    – Text explicitly evokes “primitive tradition of romance” where “a beggar was worthy of the high priestess’s hand” (ch. 11)  
    – Terrans are “choosy” for primitive difference: Skkiru’s stigma actually enhances his exotic appeal (<quote> if two eyes are beautiful, three  eyes can be fifty per cent lovelier,</quote>) (ch. 12)  
       * By performing his role well—genuine pleas, authentic “suffering,” improvised transport—he maximizes “rapport” and prospects for Larhgan’s favor.  
  b. Maintenance of Hope Sustains Motivation  
    – “All three of Larhgan’s eyes fuzzed with emotion … ‘I’m proud of you, Skkiru.’” (ch. 7)  
    – Even Bbulas “sniffed” at his progress, indicating genuine insecurities about his performance.  

Objections to Debater_B’s “Unsustainable Fallacy” Thesis

1. Gifts Are More Than Ephemeral  
  – Chocolate’s life‐saving properties encourage continued begging until local rice and fish resources (inadequate) are replaced by Terran imports.  
  – Skkiru “moodily munched” chocolate “in the wet season”—if role were futile, he’d cease trying or steal outright. His persistence shows apparent net benefit.  

2. Local Snaddrath Compliance  
  – Primitive “tabus” prevent Terrans from discovering the underground cities. If locals truly “refused alms,” the ruse fails and Terrans expose secret, ending planetary survival. Bbulas cannot risk that by starving his lone beggar.  
  – “Procession of young Snaddrath dressed in elaborate costumes … singing a ballad” (ch. 10) shows native devotion to the ritual, implying community support for all roles, including beggars.  

3. Suffering Is Part of the Act, Not Proof of Failure  
  – Temporary discomfort is necessary to maintain authenticity for anthropological study (“never before had he had to endure so much weather all at once”).  
  – The system is temporary in geologic terms but long enough to import food, fibers, and rehabilitate Snaddra’s resources. Beggarhood funds the survival of the entire population.  

4. Secret Innovation Within Role; Discipline Imposed by Bbulas  
  – Bbulas explicitly prohibits “thinking,” but Skkiru subtly subverts by using pontoons while maintaining appropriate primitive facade. This ingenuity suggests the system rewards clever beggars.  
  – If Beggar role offered no future, Bbulas would not supply the “best hut” or permit his continued presence before he dies.  

Conclusion  
Far from being an unsustainable indignity, Skkiru’s beggar caste is a calculated, resource‐rich station that grants exclusive access to Terran imports (chocolate, best hut, future trade), institutional support (pension, ceremonies), and prospects for upward mobility through “primitive” romance that he values—evidenced by his refusal to emigrate. He adapts ingeniously, demonstrates genuine gratitude, and endures only to optimize his role for both personal survival and planetary welfare. His evolving “appreciation” of beggarhood is thus the correct interpretation.
